metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.note: Definition: Cracking is the process in which large hydrocarbon molecules are broken down into smaller, more useful molecules. 3-token DDWTOS completing a cloze definition. Distractors from polymerisation and combination reaction vocabulary.

question.name: CSEC Chem Jan 2024 Q3a(i) — Define Cracking
question.text:
Define the term 'cracking' by completing the statement below:

Cracking is a process in which [[1]] hydrocarbon molecules are [[2]] into [[3]] molecules.
question.general_feedback:
Cracking: A process in which large hydrocarbon molecules are broken down into smaller molecules.

Cracking is used in the petrochemical industry to convert heavier, less useful fractions of crude oil (e.g. heavy fuel oil) into lighter, more valuable products (e.g. petrol, ethene for plastics).

Two types: thermal cracking (high temperature and pressure) and catalytic cracking (uses a catalyst at lower temperature).

ddwtos.cloze_html: Cracking is a process in which [[1]] hydrocarbon molecules are [[2]] into [[3]] molecules.

groups.label: Cracking — ___ hydrocarbon molecules
groups.diagnostic_hint: Cracking starts with LARGE (long-chain) hydrocarbon molecules — typically from the heavy fractions of crude oil such as fuel oil that are less in demand.

groups.label: Cracking — molecules are ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: The large molecules are BROKEN DOWN (cracked) — this is the reverse of polymerisation. The breaking occurs at high temperature and/or with a catalyst.

groups.label: Cracking — produces ___ molecules
groups.diagnostic_hint: Cracking produces SMALLER molecules — including short-chain alkanes (petrol) and alkenes (for plastics). This is why cracking is commercially important.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 12 tokens for 3 slots. Key distractors: 'combined' and 'polymerised' — students who confuse cracking with polymerisation (addition polymerisation joins monomers; cracking breaks chains). 'unsaturated' — students may recall that cracking produces unsaturated products (alkenes) but the INPUT molecules are saturated alkanes; this tests precision. 'heated under pressure' — this describes a METHOD of cracking, not what cracking IS (process of breaking bonds).
